title: Security Concepts
objective: Study-guide review — CISSP — Domain 1: Security and Risk Management: Security Concepts.

items: Security must support the business in achieving its goals
Security must increase the organization's value
Focus on ALL assets, not just information or data
Security is a support role — an enabler, not a blocker
Security function aligns with business strategy, goals, mission, and objectives

blocks.text: The role of security has evolved to become fully integrated with business processes. Security focuses on anything that represents value — assets — and implements controls that increase the value of those assets. From Destination CISSP: The focus of the security function is to:

items: Allow and enable the organization to achieve its goals and objectives
Increase the organization's value

blocks.text: Through proper security governance, those accountable for increasing organizational value can be supported and enabled to achieve their goals. ⚠️ Exam Trap: The CISSP exam tests the "think like a manager" mindset. Security is never about saying "no" — it's about enabling the business while managing risk. If a question gives you a choice between blocking an activity and finding a way to enable it securely, choose the enabling option. From Ahmed (How to Think Like a Manager): "To profit-driven businesses, information security is an afterthought... A manager will try to use the security program itself to not only protect company assets, but also attempt to produce measurable cost-saving results."

items: Confidentiality: Prevents unauthorized disclosure of information
Integrity: Ensures accuracy and prevents unauthorized modification
Availability: Ensures assets are accessible when needed by authorized users
Foundational model for designing all security programs
Applied to ALL assets, not just data
Confidentiality — Protects assets from unauthorized access and disclosure
Integrity — Protects assets from unauthorized or accidental changes
Availability — Protects critical assets based on value to ensure organizational assets are available when required by stakeholders

blocks.text: From Shon Harris: Some controls map to multiple CIA components. For example:

items: Availability controls: Redundant arrays (RAID), clustering, load balancing, backups
Integrity controls: Hashing, digital signatures, change management
Confidentiality controls: Encryption, access controls, data classification

blocks.title: Exam trap
blocks.text: ⚠️ Exam Trap: Shon Harris refers to the "AIC triad" (Availability, Integrity, Confidentiality) — same concept, different order. The exam uses CIA.

items: Disclosure — opposite of Confidentiality
Alteration — opposite of Integrity
Destruction/Denial — opposite of Availability
DAD represents the threats that CIA protects against
Understanding DAD helps identify which CIA component is at risk

blocks.text: The DAD triad is the inverse of CIA and represents the primary threats:

When analyzing a scenario, identify whether the threat involves disclosure (breach of confidentiality), alteration (breach of integrity), or denial/destruction (breach of availability) to determine which CIA component is at risk.

items: Authentication — Proving identity (who are you?)
Authorization — Granting permissions (what can you do?)
Accounting — Tracking actions (what did you do?)
Sometimes expanded to AAAA (adding Auditing)
Foundation for all access control systems

blocks.text: Authentication factors (the three factors of authentication):

items: Something you know — password, PIN
Something you have — smartcard, token
Something you are — biometrics (fingerprint, iris)

blocks.text: Multifactor authentication (MFA) requires two or more factors from different categories. Using two passwords is not MFA — both are "something you know." Authorization determines what resources and operations an authenticated subject can access. Authorization is granted based on identity, roles, group memberships, and security policies. Accounting/Auditing creates a record of who did what and when. This is essential for incident investigation, compliance, and non-repudiation. Audit logs must be protected from tampering.

items: Ensures a party cannot deny performing an action
Achieved through digital signatures and audit trails
Combines authentication + integrity
Critical for legal and contractual obligations
Supports accountability in security programs

blocks.text: Non-repudiation provides assurance that the sender of information cannot deny having sent it, and the recipient cannot deny having received it. This is achieved primarily through:

items: Digital signatures — Provide origin authentication and integrity
Audit trails — Record actions with timestamps and user identification
Transaction logs — Record transactions in databases and applications

blocks.text: Non-repudiation is especially important in e-commerce, legal proceedings, and regulatory compliance. Without non-repudiation, a user could claim they never authorized a transaction.
